newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan receives China's offer to return hijacker.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan receives China's offer to return hijacker.

text.p: Taiwan said on Thursday it had received a formal offer from rival China to repatriate a Taiwanese hijacker, but would not say if it would reciprocate by returning Chinese hijackers to the mainland.

The semi-official agency responsible for dialogue with communist China said it received a letter from its Beijing counterpart offering to return hijacker Liu Shan-chung to Taiwan through the arrangement of Red Cross organisations.
"We will respond to the letter in the near future," C.P. Lee, deputy secretary-general of Taiwan's state-sanctioned Straits Exchange Foundation, said on state television.
The cabinet's policymaking Mainland Affairs Council said it would accept the offer issued by Beijing's semi-official Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits.
But the council declined to give details on how it would respond to the offer.
"We accept taking back the hijacker," council vice chairman Shi Hwei-yow told the state-run Central News Agency. "The understanding we reached in the past has helped the handling of this affair."

Taiwan and China, which have not had formal links since a civil war split them in 1949, reached unofficial consensus on hijacker repatriation in 1995 but failed to sign the accord because political tensions heightened.

Shortly after Liu commandeered a Taiwan commercial jet to the mainland city of Xiamen on March 10, Taiwan publicly offered to repatriate two mainland hijackers who had completed their prison terms and asked Beijing to return Liu.
Since then Taipei has given no repatriation timetable.
Liu was the first hijacker to force a passenger plane from Taiwan to the communist mainland in the 1990s rather than the other direction.

Taipei is holding 16 mainlanders who hijacked a dozen planes to Taiwan in the early 1990s and were convicted of air piracy. In the unsigned 1995 pact with Beijing, Taipei agreed to repatriate air pirates after they serve their terms.
